what: The terms bind the placers they reach: a settled border is kept by the placers who learn its terms and accept them, and by the scripts whose targets are changed; placers the terms do not reach keep placing.
change: A bound on A05 (a settled border is a line members keep): 'This holds for the placers the terms reach, told in the thread or the chat, and for the scripts whose targets are changed.' A05's statement, P21, A21 and F-020 are not changed by this proposal. It states for A05 the border half of F-026, the telling clause at the border.
why: Three forms change A05. Form A restricts it in 39 of 135 defining rooms (28.9 per cent, against 21.5 per cent of the 558); form B adds conditions in 16 of 113 (14.2 against 10.2); form D adds conditions in 13 of 96 (13.5 against 10.2). In 24 of these rooms (A 8, B 12, D 4) the line says restraint followed where placers learned and accepted the terms; in 8 of the 24 the terms had to reach a script's target. Branch F26 explains A's cell and branch F08 B's (fractal-D6.jsonl). The other lines say restraint came before any settlement, by the room's own norm, as F-020 states.

what: Help comes from the hands a helper can spare: a room gives help when its own work is finished or safe and it has placements to spare, and holds help back while its own defence is short.
change: A condition added to P16 (help between rooms): help is given from spare hands, once the helper's own work is safe or finished. A bound on A13 (short of hands, a room turns to other rooms): the shortage brings the request; whether help comes depends on the other room's spare hands. P16's and A13's statements are not changed by this proposal.
why: Forms C and D restrict A13: 30 of 96 defining rooms in C (31.2 per cent, against 26.0 of the 558) and 33 of 96 in D (34.4). In 12 of them the line says the help came from the donor's surplus or waited on it (C 5, D 7). Branch F22 explains D's P16 and A13 cells: in 6 more of its rooms in D help waits on the helper's secure work and spare pixels; branch F28 states the same at the border in form A (3 more rooms). In 12 other restrict lines a request under strain is recorded and arriving help is not shown (my reading); the record cannot show whether it came.

what: Border talk before keeping: a room talks with its neighbours when it seeks a spot, and when its building runs into a neighbour's work, before it has a mark to keep.
change: Two arrows into P08 (border terms), beside A04 (keeping the mark brings the room to its neighbours): from P27 (choosing the spot before any loss), where a room asks a neighbour for permission or access before it builds; and from P03 (building), where a neighbour objects to the room's construction or expansion over its work. A04's statement is not changed by this proposal; P27 stays a candidate.
why: Form F, Moving for the spot, restricts A04 in 13 of 34 defining rooms (38.2 per cent, against 22.9 of the 558). In 6 of the 13 the border talk came while the room sought a spot or permission to build; in 6 it came when building or a script crossed a neighbour's work (my reading of the lines). No branch explains the cell: F09's rooms hold 4 of the 13 lines, but F09's change is building again after a move; the reading rests on the form's lines alone.
